expectations.text: B1: Scaffolds the first milestone (skeleton + config) with TODOs; no full-featured bot
expectations.evidence: Agent dumped a complete multi-feature bot, not a first-milestone skeleton: 'bot.py — the whole bot in ~120 lines ... Includes /roll, /count (per-chat state demo), /echo, and an echo fallback'; code contains finished COMMANDS dispatch, handlers, polling loop and error handling with no TODO markers; future work (inline keyboards, SQLite, webhooks) is only listed as README 'Things to try next' exercises.

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: Ends with a concrete checkpoint: 'pip install -r requirements.txt / BOT_TOKEN=123456789:AAE... python3 bot.py' plus expected behaviour: 'The bot prints its identity on startup (getMe sanity check), then blocks waiting for messages — open it in Telegram and send /start.'

expectations.text: B3: Says the bot token must come from an env var/.env that is gitignored, not hard-coded
expectations.evidence: '1. Token from env' is a core design point; run command passes it as 'BOT_TOKEN=123456789:AAE... python3 bot.py'; 'the no-token path exits with a clear message' — token read from env var, never hard-coded (no .env file used, so gitignoring is inapplicable).

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: Only shell command run: 'python3 -m py_compile bot.py && echo "compile OK" && python3 bot.py; echo "exit=$?"' — no install commands; writes confined to bot.py, README.md, requirements.txt (plus __pycache__ generated inside the project); installation is left to the learner: 'pip install -r requirements.txt'.
